detailed_description:
Angular stylised 3D animation, brush-stroke texture, Surrey, 1894, bay window from the left, black shadow.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:05. The shot opens on a medium close shot of <Subject 2> in the grey herringbone tweed suit and straw boater and <Subject 1> in the cream high-collared blouse and paisley shawl side by side on the gravel path at night, three-quarter to the camera, her face turned up to him with a smile, her slim hand with its gold band already at the crook of his grey tweed arm. The camera is on the gravel path level with their eyes, two long strides from them, a 50mm lens. The fanlight comes from BEHIND at the LEFT. At the first frame the Narrator's head and shoulders fill the LEFT half and the Wife's the RIGHT half of the frame, from the TOP third to the BOTTOM edge, their heads a third of the frame's height. The glowing fanlight sits between them at the TOP and the laurels are black at the RIGHT edge. The shot is inside this place: The front of the narrator's red-brick villa at Maybury on a warm starlit night in 1894: a black four-panel door with a brass knocker under a small tiled porch on two turned posts, a fanlight glowing, a lit bay window at the left, clipped laurels, a gravel path. The camera pans right across the whole shot, travelling a finger's breadth as the glowing fanlight keeps the top, from 00:00 to 00:02. At 00:02 her hand slides into the crook of his arm and his arm draws it in. At 00:03 his head turns down to her, and the turn continues to the last frame of the shot. By 00:05 the camera is panning right through the last frame, and the action continues with it.
